facts.statement: Abydosaurus is a brachiosaurid sauropod dinosaur known from fossils found in the Upper Lower Cretaceous rocks of northeastern Utah, United States.
facts.quote: Abydosaurus (meaning "Abydos lizard") is a genus of brachiosaurid sauropod dinosaur known from skull and postcranial material found in upper Lower Cretaceous rocks of northeastern Utah, United States.

facts.statement: The genus Abydosaurus was named in 2010 by Daniel Chure and colleagues.
facts.quote: Abydosaurus was named in 2010 by Daniel Chure and colleagues.

facts.statement: The type species A. mcintoshi was named in honor of John S. McIntosh for his contributions to Dinosaur National Monument and sauropod research.
facts.quote: The type species is A. mcintoshi in honor of John S. ("Jack") McIntosh, Professor of Physics, Emeritus, Wesleyan University, and his contributions to Dinosaur National Monument and the study of sauropod dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Fossils of Abydosaurus date to the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, with an age of less than 104.46 ± 0.95 million years.
facts.quote: Zircons from mudstones beneath the bone-bearing sandstone indicate the age of the sandstone and its contained bones is less than 104.46 ± 0.95 million years, in the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen DINO 16488 consists of a nearly complete skull, lower jaws, and the first four neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: Abydosaurus is based on the holotype DINO 16488, a nearly complete skull and lower jaws with the first four neck vertebrae.

facts.statement: Abydosaurus is notable for having narrow teeth, contrasting with the broader teeth of earlier brachiosaurids.
facts.quote: It is also notable for its narrow teeth, as earlier brachiosaurids had broader teeth.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz estimated the length of Abydosaurus to be 18.3 meters in 2012.
facts.quote: In 2012 Thomas Holtz gave a length of 18.3 m.

facts.statement: Four skulls of Abydosaurus are known, two of which are very complete, all measuring approximately 50 cm in length and 25 cm in height.
facts.quote: Se conocen 4 cráneos de este dinosaurio, 2 de ellos muy completos, todos ellos son de aproximadamente del mismo tamaño, de unos 50 cm de largo y 25 de alto.

facts.statement: Abydosaurus measured approximately 25 meters in length, 6.5 meters in height, and weighed 25 tons.
facts.quote: El dinosaurio medía aproximadamente 25 metros de largo, 6,5 de alto y pesaba 25 toneladas.

facts.statement: Although Abydosaurus lived about 45 million years after Giraffatitan, their skulls are similar except for Abydosaurus having narrower, sharper teeth and a smaller nose.
facts.quote: Aunque Abydosaurus vivió cerca de 45 millones de años después de Giraffatitan, los cráneos de ambos géneros son similares excepto por los dientes más estrechos y afilados, que contrastan con los anchos dientes de los braquiosáuridos anteriores, y la nariz más pequeña de Abydosaurus.

facts.statement: Abydosaurus can be distinguished from other sauropods, including Giraffatitan, by subtle features of the nasal and maxillary bones, relatively small external nares, and specific dental characteristics.
facts.quote: Abydosaurus puede ser diferenciado de otros saurópodos, incluyendo a Giraffatitan, por rasgos sutiles del hueso nasal y de los huesos maxilares, sus fosas nasales externas relativamente pequeñas, y algunas características de los dientes.

facts.statement: The name Abydosaurus references Abydos, the mythical location where the head and neck of the god Osiris were preserved.
facts.quote: El nombre hace referencia a Abidos, el lugar donde mitológicamente se conservaron el cráneo y el cuello del dios Osiris.

facts.statement: Abydosaurus is classified within the family Brachiosauridae.
The genus authority for Abydosaurus is Chure et al., 2010.
The parent group of the genus Abydosaurus is Brachiosauridae.
The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Abydosaurus as the Cenomanian, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Abydosaurus is notable for being one of the few sauropods known from skull material and holds the record for the first described complete skull of a Cretaceous sauropod from the Americas.
rejected.quote: Abydosaurus is one of the few sauropods known from skull material, with the first described complete skull for a Cretaceous sauropod from the Americas.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'one of the few sauropods known from skull'

rejected.quote: Abundant skull and postcranial bones were found at the same site, including partial skulls from three additional individuals, a partial hip and associated tail vertebrae, a shoulder blade, an upper arm bone, and hand bones.
